name: Kanazawa
tagline: The Maeda clan's city: winter crab, Kaga court cooking and a 300-year-old market.
history: Kanazawa was the capital of the Kaga domain, ruled by the Maeda clan: the richest fief in Edo Japan after the shogunate itself. Unable to spend on an army without raising suspicion in Edo, the Maeda spent on tea, lacquer, sweets and the table. That gave us Kaga ryōri: court dishes served on Kutani porcelain and Wajima lacquer, and duck jibuni, which already appears in an 18th-century recipe book by a cook in the Maeda's service.

Gold is the other legacy. About 99% of Japan's gold leaf is beaten here (Kanazawa-haku). The domain kept beating gold in secret while the shogunate held the monopoly, and the humid climate and the region's lacquer and Buddhist-altar workshops did the rest. Hence the gold-leaf ice cream in Higashi Chaya: it's decoration, it tastes of nothing.

The Sea of Japan feeds the city. Ōmichō market dates itself from 1721 (its roots go back to a fire in 1690 that brought the fishmongers together there), supplied the domain's kitchen and today has close to 170 stalls. From the land come the Kaga yasai: 15 certified vegetables, grown since before 1945 and still planted in Kanazawa, such as gensuke radish, Kaga lotus root and purple kinjisō.
winter: December is kōbako-gani month: the female snow crab, with roe inside and out. The season opens on 6 Nov and Ishikawa closes it for females historically ~29 Dec (2026 date to confirm), so kōbako means being here before ~28 Dec. For us that means our first two nights, 27 and 28 Dec, with the 29th a maybe. The male (加能ガニ) runs until March. It's also the season for fatty buri, kabura-zushi and gensuke radish in the oden.

meibutsu.name: Kōbako crab
meibutsu.what: A small female zuwai crab, boiled whole: orange inner roe (uchiko), granular outer roe (sotoko) and the miso. Taken apart in its shell and eaten with tosa vinegar. Only around from 6 Nov to historically ~29 Dec (2026 date to confirm).
meibutsu.where: Yamasan Sushi and Kabuna; in winter Miyuki's oden adds kani-men; Otome Zushi at the top end.
meibutsu.pregnancy_note: For Fernanda: cooked, so fine. Only skip kani-sashi (raw crab) if it turns up.
meibutsu.glance: Small female snow crab, boiled, packed with two kinds of roe.
meibutsu.story: This crab has a deadline. Ishikawa opens the season on 6 November and closes it for females historically ~29 Dec (2026 date to confirm), so our first nights here are the window. Kōbako is the small female snow crab, boiled whole. Inside the shell you'll find orange inner roe, granular outer roe and the crab's miso. Take it apart piece by piece and dip it in tosa vinegar. It's cooked, so Fernanda joins in.

meibutsu.name: Jibuni
meibutsu.what: Sliced duck dusted in flour and simmered in dashi, soy and mirin with sudare-fu (Kanazawa wheat gluten), shiitake and greens. The flour thickens the broth; it's eaten with wasabi. The emblem of Kaga cooking.
meibutsu.where: Kabuna; Gyohan (魚半), where Mark Wiens had jibuni for ¥2,800 (Tabelog not checked).
meibutsu.pregnancy_note: Duck cooked through in the broth. All fine for Fernanda.
meibutsu.glance: Duck simmered in a thick, gentle broth.
meibutsu.story: The Maeda lords couldn't spend on an army without raising suspicion in Edo, so they spent on tea, lacquer, sweets and the table. Jibuni is the emblem of the Kaga court cooking that came out of it, already written down in an 18th-century recipe book by one of the Maeda's cooks. Sliced duck is dusted in flour and simmered with sudare-fu gluten, shiitake and greens; the flour thickens the broth. Eat it with a little wasabi.

meibutsu.name: Kanazawa oden
meibutsu.what: Clear-broth oden eaten all year round, with local pieces: kuruma-fu (gluten wheels), bai-gai (whelk), gensuke radish and, in season, kani-men with kōbako crab.
meibutsu.where: Oden Izakaya Miyuki and Akadama, both in Katamachi.
meibutsu.pregnancy_note: All cooked. For Fernanda: skip only raw shellfish served on the side.
meibutsu.glance: Clear-broth oden eaten year-round, with local pieces like gluten wheels.
meibutsu.story: Kanazawa eats oden all year round. Its two classic houses are Akadama, open since 1927, and Miyuki, since 1967, with a lighter, cleaner dashi. The broth is clear and the pieces are local: kuruma-fu (wheels of wheat gluten), bai-gai (whelk), gensuke radish, one of the certified Kaga vegetables, and, in winter, kani-men made with kōbako crab. Order a few pieces at a time and keep going.

meibutsu.name: Winter buri
meibutsu.what: Fatty winter yellowtail from the Sea of Japan, as sashimi, sushi, teriyaki or buri-daikon.
meibutsu.glance: Fatty winter yellowtail, raw or cooked, at its December peak.
meibutsu.pregnancy_note: Cooked (teriyaki, buri-daikon) is fine; raw as sashimi or sushi: a few pieces at a good counter.

meibutsu.name: Kabura-zushi
meibutsu.what: A winter pickle: slices of turnip with salted buri in between, fermented in rice kōji. One of the city's New Year gifts.
meibutsu.where: Ōmichō stalls and the station gift shops (Hyakubangai).
meibutsu.pregnancy_note: The buri is cured and fermented, not cooked. Better for Fernanda to taste only the turnip, or pass.
meibutsu.glance: Turnip and salted yellowtail fermented in rice kōji; a New Year gift.

meibutsu.name: Grilled nodoguro
meibutsu.what: A red fish with very rich flesh (akamutsu), salt-grilled. One of the Hokuriku's pricey dishes.
meibutsu.glance: A rich red fish, salt-grilled; one of Hokuriku's pricey treats.

meibutsu.name: Kanazawa curry
meibutsu.what: Thick dark sauce covering the rice, katsu on top, shredded cabbage on the side, a metal fork and a stainless-steel plate. Turban, from 1971, is held to be the original.
meibutsu.where: Turban Curry Honten (Mark Wiens filmed there).
meibutsu.glance: Thick dark curry over rice, katsu on top, on a steel plate.

meibutsu.name: Amanattō and wagashi
meibutsu.what: A tea-ceremony city is a sweets city. Candied beans from Kawamura and kanmi in Higashi Chaya.
meibutsu.glance: Candied beans and tea sweets from a tea-ceremony city.

areas.name: Ōmichō Market
areas.story: A market since 1721 that supplied the Kaga domain's kitchen. Today close to 170 stalls of fish, crab, Kaga vegetables and kaisen-don counters.
eat: A stall croquette (Mark Wiens tried one)
areas.tips: Get there before 8:00 for Ikiiki-tei. Most kaisen-don stalls sit at 3.40–3.49 on Tabelog: be choosy and check crab prices by weight.
areas.dec_jan: 28–30 Dec is the New Year shopping rush: packed, with crab sold by the box. That covers every market day we have after Sun 27 Dec, our arrival day and the one calm visit, if we get in early enough. On the 28th we're in Shirakawa-go; on the 29th and the morning of the 30th, go early, eat at a counter and don't plan to browse. We leave on the 30th, so the New Year closure doesn't touch us (in 2024–25 it opened 31 Dec with short hours and closed 1–3 Jan; 2026–27 calendar to confirm, 076-231-1462).
areas.glance: Kanazawa's 300-year-old fish market: crab, buri and seafood bowls.

areas.name: Higashi Chaya
areas.story: The old geisha teahouse district of wooden houses, now full of sweet shops, tea and gold-leaf shops.
eat: Matcha (Mark Wiens stopped at a teahouse here)
Gold-leaf ice cream (for the photo, not the taste)
areas.tips: Empty early in the morning. The gold-leaf shops are touristy; the sweets are what's worth it.
areas.dec_jan: Kawamura's shop is open on our dates (it closes 31 Dec–3 Jan), but its upstairs salon is closed 24 Dec–4 Jan. Tsubomi closes Wednesdays, so not on 30 Dec.
areas.glance: Old geisha teahouse lanes; come for the sweets, not the gold.

areas.name: Katamachi and Kiguramachi
areas.story: The night-time centre: oden, izakaya and the expensive sushi counters.
areas.tips: Book oden and izakaya ahead for seven.
areas.dec_jan: Many close on Sundays, and Sun 27 Dec is our first night: plan the big dinners for Mon 28 (after Shirakawa-go) and Tue 29 Dec. Year-end hours to confirm.
areas.glance: The night-time centre: oden, izakaya and serious sushi counters.

places.name: Ikiiki-tei Ōmichō
places.name_ja: いきいき亭 近江町店

critics.note: Breakfast at Ōmichō: a ¥3,500 kaisen-don here.

places.why: The market counter that cares about the fish, not the photo. The 'Local' bowl uses only local catch, and the rice and toppings come separately.
places.pregnancy_note: The raw bowl has amaebi, gasuebi, scallop and sea urchin. For Fernanda: ask for fish only, no crustaceans or shellfish, or she eats elsewhere.
places.group: 10 counter seats. Split 4+3 (or 3+2+2) over two rounds.
places.booking: No reservations. Put a name on the list at opening (7:00). By midday the wait reaches ~2 h.
places.dec_jan: 7:00–15:00, closed Tuesdays (29 Dec). Our chances: Sun 27 Dec if we arrive before 15:00, before the rush, or the 7:00 list on Wed 30 Dec before the Kyoto train, in the thick of it. It probably follows the market's 1–3 Jan closure (to confirm), but we've gone by then.
places.glance: Ōmichō's best market counter; order the local-catch bowl.

places.name: Yamasan Sushi Honten
places.why: The market sushi place with room for a group. The best bet for a lunch of kōbako and buri.
places.pregnancy_note: Boiled kōbako and other cooked pieces are fine. Raw buri and other fish nigiri: a few pieces; no shellfish.
places.group: 32 seats on tatami and at tables; book for seven and check they'll seat us together.
places.booking: Online booking for a few groups a day.
places.dec_jan: 9:00–16:00, no fixed closing day, so it works on Sun 27 Dec, when the Katamachi places are shut: our kōbako lunch on arrival day, before the season ends (historically ~29 Dec (2026 date to confirm)) and before the market rush. Year-end hours to confirm.
places.glance: Market sushi with room for seven; kōbako and buri lunch.

places.name: Otome Zushi

tabelog.awards: Tabelog Award Bronze 2020–2026, Silver 2019; 寿司 WEST 百名店 2021, 2022, 2025

places.why: Kanazawa's historic benchmark: Hokuriku fish handled with restraint. Lunch is the cheapest way in.
places.order: Omakase; in winter, buri and kōbako.
places.pregnancy_note: For Fernanda: ask ahead to swap raw shellfish and shirako (likely in December) for cooked pieces. Boiled kōbako is fine; raw buri and other nigiri, a few pieces.
places.group: 17 seats: a 9-seat counter and an 8-seat tatami room. For seven, book the tatami room (7 of its 8 seats), or 4+3 across counter sittings.
places.booking: Online, opens 2 months ahead. Book in late October.
places.dec_jan: Lunch and dinner; closed Wednesdays, Sundays and holidays, so only Mon 28 (dinner, after Shirakawa-go) and Tue 29 Dec work for us. With kōbako ending historically ~29 Dec (2026 date to confirm), the 28th is the safer night. Year-end hours to confirm.

critics.note: Posted from here in Feb 2016 (post embedded in Tokyo Table Trip).

places.glance: Kanazawa's benchmark sushi; winter crab and yellowtail.

places.name: Kabuna

tabelog.awards: 居酒屋 WEST 百名店 2025, 2026

places.why: The local-cooking izakaya that Tabelog reviewers keep returning to for the jibuni and the seasonal crab.
places.pregnancy_note: Wide menu. For Fernanda: skip raw shellfish and shirako.
places.group: 11 private rooms, including one for 6: ask whether a seventh chair fits, or for a bigger room. The best group dinner under ¥10k in town.
places.dec_jan: Closed Sundays, so not 27 Dec. Mon 28 or Tue 29 Dec; take the 28th if we want kōbako while it lasts. Year-end hours to confirm.
places.glance: Local-cooking izakaya: jibuni, oden, nodoguro and seasonal crab.

places.name: Oden Izakaya Miyuki
places.name_ja: おでん居酒屋 三幸
places.why: Since 1967. Lighter, cleaner dashi than its rival Akadama, and a genuinely local crowd.
places.order: Miyuki-age (the house satsuma-age), kuruma-fu, bai-gai, radish; kani-men in season.
places.pregnancy_note: All cooked. For Fernanda: skip only raw shellfish sides.
places.dec_jan: 16:00–22:00; closed Sundays, holidays and the 2nd Monday of the month (11 Jan 2027 closed, after we've gone). So not Sun 27 Dec; Mon 28 and Tue 29 Dec aren't closing days, and kani-men only while kōbako lasts (historically ~29 Dec (2026 date to confirm)). Year-end hours to confirm.
places.glance: Since 1967: clean-broth Kanazawa oden with a local crowd.

places.name: Turban Curry Honten
places.name_ja: ターバンカレー 本店

critics.note: Tried Kanazawa curry here in his city video.

places.why: The 1971 original, which Tabelog reviewers call 本家本元. Under 3.5: it's here for the history.
places.dec_jan: Closed 30 Dec–1 Jan (it reopens on 2 Jan), so go 27–29 Dec, not on the morning we leave.
places.glance: The 1971 original Kanazawa curry: thick sauce, katsu, steel plate.

places.name: Kataori

critics.note: Miso dengaku with kinome, yomogi tofu and umeboshi ochazuke with okoge (Jun 2024).
Been once (Sep 2020), per the City Foodsters visit log.

places.why: The highest score in the whole guide (4.70), and Meg names it among her places of purity and simplicity.
places.pregnancy_note: For Fernanda: say so when booking and ask for cooked dishes.
places.group: 8-seat counter: book 7 of its 8 seats (in effect the whole counter), or 4+3.
places.glance: The guide's top score (4.70): pure, simple Kanazawa kaiseki.

places.name: Kisanuki

critics.note: Been once (Jun 2025), per the City Foodsters visit log.

places.why: A new Kanazawa kaiseki already above 4.5 on Tabelog.
places.pregnancy_note: For Fernanda: say so when booking and ask for cooked dishes.
places.glance: A new Kanazawa kaiseki already above 4.5 on Tabelog.

places.name: Sushi Dokoro Mekumi

critics.note: Been once (Apr 2017), per the City Foodsters visit log.

places.why: Hokuriku-fish sushi with Tabelog gold, out of the centre.
places.pregnancy_note: Almost all raw: for Fernanda, say so when booking.
places.glance: Gold-award sushi of Hokuriku fish, just outside Kanazawa.

shops.name: Amanatto Kawamura
shops.what: Candied beans (amanattō) from a Higashi Chaya sweet house. Tabelog 3.73, 和菓子 WEST 百名店 2023, 2026.
shops.buy: Boxes of amanattō, which travel well as gifts.
shops.dec_jan: Shop open on our dates (closed 31 Dec–3 Jan); upstairs salon closed 24 Dec–4 Jan, so no sitting down.

shops.name: Tsubomi
shops.what: A kanmi house (sweets and tea) in Higashi Chaya. Tabelog 3.66, 和菓子 WEST 百名店 2023, 2026.
shops.dec_jan: Closed Wednesdays (30 Dec, our leaving day). Year-end hours to confirm.

shops.name: Suzume Kanazawa Hyakubangai
shops.name_ja: すゞめ 金沢百番街店
shops.what: A wagashi shop inside the station, on the 和菓子 百名店 2026 list.
shops.dec_jan: To confirm; handy on 30 Dec for the train to Kyoto.

shops.name: Fukumitsuya
shops.what: A Kanazawa sake brewery, in full production in December.
shops.buy: Sake for the men; kōji amazake (alcohol-free) for Fernanda, if they have it.
shops.dec_jan: Shop hours at the year end to confirm.
